newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador gov't wants new tax on cable TV, cellphones.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador gov't wants new tax on cable TV, cellphones.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon presented an urgent bill in Congress late on Wednesday which would slap a new "Special Consumer Tax" on toys, cable television and mobile telephones.

Fabian, announcing the bill for a new five percent tax on toys and 10 percent on cable TV and cellphones, told a news conference: "The tax on cellphones would mean $100 million a year income to the state."

He did not give further details of the new taxes, but said cigarettes, liquors and other alcoholic drinks would have the special tax reduced, from the 100 percent increases slapped on them by the ousted former President Abdala Bucaram.
There were other smaller special tax decreases, with the special tax on cars falling to 5.0 percent from 10 percent.
